analysis: What changed vs the 7 AM brief: the slide has moderated slightly off the worst levels — S&P -2.7% vs -3.05% at the open, Nasdaq -3.9% vs -4.41% — but SPY is still below $700 ($698.30) and the tape is printing near the lows into a thin Thanksgiving week. The tariff story softened in tone but not in substance: Greer's CNBC appearance framed the rates as top-ups on existing duties with roughly $30B of Chinese goods exempt and nothing taking effect for a couple of months, which undercuts the worst-case read without removing the overhang. The genuinely new item is Trump floating a US equity stake in Nvidia (plus a possible Huang pardon) — a fresh political overhang on the market's most important stock, with the Intel ~10% stake as the precedent. Deere rallying ~4% on an EPS miss and a below-consensus FY27 guide is the one counter-trend signal: the market is rewarding non-AI cyclicals even on weak numbers. The structural damage marker is SMH, down 6% for its ninth loss in 10 sessions and now more than 40% below its summer peak. Signal vs noise: SPY below $700, the SMH drawdown, the hot PCE print and the confirmed tariff proposal are signal; the exact intraday percentages and any single-name bounce are noise. The risk into the close is the same as this morning — thin holiday tape amplifying the first move in either direction.

community_signals.takeaway: WSB sentiment remains at extreme fear (~8-12/100). NVDA is now treated as a 'meme coin' — the reinstatement rally is called the biggest bull trap ever, with bearish targets shifted down to 135/125/120. The new split in the thread: some users are averaging down on MU, AMD, NVDA and GOOGL ('enjoy this insane fire sale'), while the dominant tone is still selling and puts. Community panic still exceeds the actual decline (SPY -2.75% vs the -7% circuit-breaker threshold).

headlines.headline: Indexes off the worst levels but still deep red near mid-morning: S&P 500 -2.7%, Nasdaq Composite -3.9%, Dow -1.7% (more than 800 points). SPY $698.30 (-2.85% as of 10:47 AM ET), still below $700 after an intraday low of $698.53. Russell 2000 down more than 2%. VIX just under 32, up ~21%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The gap-down is holding, not reversing — the modest bounce off the open's lows still leaves the S&P below $700 with tech leading the downside into a thin Thanksgiving-week tape.

headlines.headline: Trump floats a US government equity stake in Nvidia — and a possible pardon for CEO Jensen Huang — in a New York Post interview: 'I thought about it... It's probably not too late.' He noted Intel handed over a near-10% stake after he demanded its CEO's resignation. Huang faces congressional hearings Dec 1 (closed-door, three House committees) and Dec 3 (public, Senate). NVDA down ~8% to ~$142.90.
headlines.why_it_matters: A new political overhang on the market's most important stock — state ownership would be a precedent-setting step for a private chipmaker, and it lands on top of the AI unwind. Earnings context: Nov 17, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B expected (+103% y/y).

headlines.headline: Greer softens the tariff read on CNBC: the proposed Section 301 rates would mostly 'top up' existing duties rather than stack in full, with about $30B of Chinese goods exempt, and he does not expect any to take effect 'for at least a couple of months.' Written comments due Jan 5, 2027, hearings from Jan 25, 2027. Separately, USTR proposed a 10% tariff on finished Brazilian aircraft and higher out-of-quota sugar tariffs, with comments due Dec 30 and a hearing Jan 14, 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: The top-up framing and the months-long timeline undercut the worst-case tariff read, but the proposal is still live and multi-month — the overhang is delayed, not removed. Specific rates are due in a Federal Register notice Wednesday.

headlines.headline: Deere rallies ~3.7-3.9% to ~$637 despite an earnings miss: fiscal Q4 EPS $3.89 vs $4.03 FactSet expected, net sales $10.51B vs $10.38B expected, and FY27 net income guidance of $4.5-5.25B below Wall Street estimates. Large-ag sales slid 15% to $4.02B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The one counter-trend signal in the tape — a non-AI cyclical rising on a miss and a weak guide shows the market is rewarding anything outside the AI complex, a rotation pattern worth watching into the close.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps all red with Alphabet at a new 52-week low: GOOGL -5.4% to ~$264, Amazon -5%, Tesla -5%, Meta -3.6%, Microsoft -3.7%; Apple the relative holdout at -1.7%. The Mag 7 group is down 4.56%, accounting for about 1.40 points of the S&P's decline.
headlines.why_it_matters: No mega-cap is escaping and the most AI-exposed names are down most — the weakness is concentrated in the leadership that carried the market, which is what makes the index move so large.

headlines.headline: Semiconductors keep breaking down: SMH -6%, its ninth loss in 10 sessions, trading near $399 — more than 40% below its summertime peak of $671.83. SOXX -7%; Astera Labs and Micron each down ~9-10.6%; Broadcom -6%; AMD, Intel, Marvell, Applied Materials and Arm each down more than 7-8%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The chip complex is now in a deep drawdown from its summer peak, not a pullback — the epicenter of the selloff is getting worse, and it is dragging the whole AI trade with it.

headlines.headline: Dell down ~10% and still falling after its record quarter: shares hit a low of $137.72, the lowest since April 7, despite adjusted EPS $9.45 vs ~$6.59 consensus, revenue $54.94B vs $49.32B expected, and raised full-year guidance. HPE down ~4-6% after sinking 16% Tuesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat-and-fall pattern is now the rule — even a record quarter with a raised guide is being sold, so the market is judging valuation and AI-demand durability, not the quarter itself.

headlines.headline: Defensives are the only green: Procter & Gamble and Coca-Cola each +0.8%, consumer staples ETF XLP +0.1%, and Nasdaq-100 gainers Paychex +1.9% and Mondelez +1.4%. Earnings movers elsewhere: Ambarella -33%, Autodesk -5%, Workday -5%, HP modestly higher. October durable-goods orders +0.2% vs 0.5% expected.
headlines.why_it_matters: Classic risk-off rotation — money is hiding in staples and dividend payers while growth gets sold, and the durable-goods miss adds a small soft-data note to the hot-inflation morning.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) — revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M, DCF $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Nov 24 Zacks analysis highlights the $500M order book through 2029, with >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted and revenue per horsepower +8% y/y. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027. WTI ~$82.60 (+1%) is a small tailwind for the energy complex.
